result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

result.rule: When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives or says an activity may or may not occur, and the paths later continue in common: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway, and reconnect the alternative paths with an exclusive merge before their shared continuation.
When the description states that a condition determines whether an action or process path is needed: model the choice with an exclusive gateway and conditional branches for the possible outcomes.

When the description says an activity may or may not take place: Model the choice with an exclusive split: one path performs the optional activity and the other bypasses it. Rejoin the alternative paths with an exclusive merge when both continue into the same flow.

When the description states a distinct handling action to be performed after an item or material is received: Model that handling action as a BPMN activity in the described flow; do not omit it or absorb it into another activity.
